sentences.text: Porphyrio claytongreenei was described by Worthy and colleagues.
Fossils of this bird have been recovered from New Zealand.
The specific name honors Warren Clayton-Greene, the landowner who protected the fossil site by fencing it off from livestock.
The species is placed in the genus Porphyrio, a group of swamphens within the rail family Rallidae.
Its specific epithet is claytongreenei, and Worthy et al. formally named it in 2026.
The bird lived during the Pleistocene epoch, specifically in the Calabrian stage of Zealandia.
The genus Porphyrio has a fossil record extending from the Zanclean to the Holocene, spanning 5.333 million to 0 years ago.
